states.name: out
states.meaning: 32-bit sticky capture register; out[i] becomes 1 after in[i] is sampled as 1 in one cycle and 0 in the next, and remains 1 until synchronous reset.
states.update_time: posedge after sampling reset and in; reset has priority and sets all bits to 0

states.name: prev_in
states.meaning: 32-bit previous sampled value of in, used to detect per-bit 1-to-0 transitions; it tracks in on every posedge including reset cycles.

rules.condition: reset == 1; on this posedge out becomes 32'd0.
reset == 0 and exists i such that prev_in[i] == 1 and in[i] == 0; for each bit j, out[j] becomes 1 if prev_in[j] == 1 and in[j] == 0, else out[j] holds its previous value.
rules.spec_quote: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next

rules.condition: reset == 0 and for all i, not (prev_in[i] == 1 and in[i] == 0); for each bit j, out[j] holds its previous value.
rules.spec_quote: output will remain 1 until the register is reset

reset.name: reset
reset.first_released_cycle: the first posedge that samples reset == 0; normal capture/hold behavior applies on that same edge after reset is released

before.mid: mid may specify nonclock input changes applied after the row's posedge sampling and before the next edge; those changes become the start values for the next row unless the next row explicitly overrides them.

uncertain.note: Whether prev_in should track in during reset cycles is unspecified; under the current contract, a 1 sampled while reset is high can pair with a 0 after release and set out.
candidates: prev_in tracks in on every posedge including reset cycles; a 1 sampled while reset is high followed by 0 after release captures (current behavior)
prev_in is cleared or ignored while reset is high, so reset-cycle history cannot cause capture after release
